answer: Each PoA identity must complete a VDF chain of sequential modular squarings, with each result determining the next; a Wesolowski proof lets peers verify the work efficiently. An attacker can mirror identities, but each clone needs its own chain: GPUs can process chains in parallel, not collapse the dependency within one chain. Thus cloning increases hardware demand, while the sequential work imposes a physical time floor—the nadir of throughput—rather than a plume of cost-free identities.
